CausalChain: Nanoparticle-mediated liver targeting → Efficient delivery of dual gene therapy payload → CRISPR/Cas9 knock-out of PD-L1 in tumor cells reduces local immunosuppression → Concurrent expression of IL-12 enhances T cell activation → Reinvigorated cytotoxic T cells overcome tumor resistance → Enhanced tumor clearance in HCC
Hypothesis: Co-delivery of a CRISPR/Cas9 construct targeting PD-L1 along with an IL-12 gene via liver-targeted nanoparticles will synergistically overcome the immunosuppressive microenvironment of hepatocellular carcinoma, thereby enhancing anti-tumor immune responses and improving therapeutic outcomes in advanced HCC.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) continues to be characterized by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that limits the efficacy of conventional therapeutic approaches. Recent advances in gene therapy, nanoparticle‐mediated delivery systems, and immunomodulation have highlighted exciting opportunities to overcome these therapeutic hurdles. Here, we propose a novel strategy that combines targeted, nonviral nanoparticle delivery of a dual gene therapy payload – a CRISPR/Cas9 system designed to inactivate PD‐L1 expression in HCC tumor cells and an immunostimulatory cytokine gene (interleukin‐12) to enhance local T cell activation. This integrated approach is designed to both disrupt the tumor’s innate immunosuppressive mechanisms and boost cytotoxic T cell responses, potentially synergizing with existing immunotherapeutic regimens and improving overall treatment efficacy.
